# Plan: unattended SPE rounds, starting with round 5

## Summary
I will run SPE rounds one after another tonight, starting with round 5. Each round goes through specify, predict, evaluate, and learn. I make a local commit after each step. I will not push, open PRs, deploy, or send messages. I stop when the first stop rule fires. When I stop, I write a report in chat for you to read in the morning.

## Caps you approve with this plan
You did not give a round cap or a budget. I propose the caps below. Change any number before you approve.

| Cap | Proposed value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Max rounds tonight | 4 (r05 to r08) | Each round needs a real design change. Four is more than the proposals usually support. |
| Spend per round | 2x the measured cost of round 4 | This leaves room for harder tasks without letting one round run away. |
| Total spend tonight | 6x the measured cost of round 4 | This is a hard stop even if rounds remain. |
| Workflow wall time | 2x round 4's measured wall time per run | A run past this point is treated as hung. I halt and report it. |
| Loop time | No new round starts after 6 hours | You get the report before you are back. |

## Stop rules (end the loop and report)
1. Predictions match results within their stated error for 3 rounds in a row. Rounds 2 to 4 count toward this. I report that the design is stable enough to judge for go-live.
2. A cap in the table above is reached.
3. A failure or proposal needs a decision only you can make. See the list below.
4. The next round's only proposal is "more trials". More trials is not a design change, so that round would measure nothing new.

## Halt rules (stop mid-round and report)
- A budget cap is hit during a run.
- An answer key leaks into a trial's prompt, files, or tools.
- A grader is found broken during a run. I keep the raw results and do not regrade until the next round.

## What I may change alone, and what waits for you
I may do these alone:
- Apply items from the last round's "Proposed for round N+1" table when they stay inside the current requirements.
- Make tasks harder or graders stricter when every configuration passed everything.
- Fix harness bugs. I log each fix as a failure entry.
- Fix a grader between rounds. I disclose the regrade in the log and keep the original numbers next to the regraded ones.

These wait for you:
- Any change to a requirement whose source is your own words.
- Any change to the go-live threshold.
- Adding a configuration that costs more per task, such as a new model.
- Raising any cap.
- Deleting or rewriting results, predictions, or log entries from earlier rounds.

One more rule keeps the author away from the judge. I never change a grader and the thing it grades in the same round.

## Round 5

### Specify
- Inputs are the "Proposed for round 5" table at the end of `spe/spec/spec.md` and the open entries in `spe/failures.md`.
- I write a requirement table with the columns ID, Requirement, Source, and Test. Every new row cites one of your quotes, a recorded decision, or a failure ID such as F3.
- Your message tonight goes into `spe/spec/transcripts/r05-overnight.md`. It is the only new user input for every round tonight.
- Commit: `SPE r05 specify: <the main change>`.

### Predict
- I have not read round 4's measured values while writing this plan. So the round 5 cells are not filled here. I fill them from `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml` right after you approve, and before any harness work.
- The table has one row per metric and one column per configuration, plus a "Same as last round" column. The metrics are pass rate, tool calls per task, cost per task, and wall time per task.
- Every cell is a number with an error band, such as "88% pass, plus or minus 5 points". Every row has a one-line Why and names the grader check that measures it.
- I save the plan to `spe/plans/r05.md` and the numbers to `spe/predictions/r05.yaml`.
- Commit: `SPE r05 predict: <one-line prediction headline>`. No trial runs before this commit.

### Evaluate
Each build step has a gate. I do not move on until the gate passes.

| Step | Gate |
|---|---|
| 1. Build `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js` from the round 4 harness plus the specified changes | The script loads with no errors. |
| 2. Self-test each grader on one known-good and one known-bad sample | Every grader passes the good sample and fails the bad sample. |
| 3. Leak check on every trial prompt and workspace | A search for answer-key content finds zero hits. |
| 4. Dry run with 1 trial per configuration | Results land in `spe/evals/results/r05/` and every result is graded. |

- Commit: `SPE r05 evaluate (harness): <what changed>`.
- Workflow arguments use the same trial count as round 4 unless the round 5 spec changes it.
- Cost and time estimate is round 4's measured cost and time, scaled by trial count. This estimate is unmeasured.
- The Workflow returns at launch. I wait for its completion notice before grading.
- Commit: `SPE r05 evaluate (results): <headline numbers>`.

### Close-out (learn)
- I add a round 5 section to `spe/prediction-log.md` with the columns Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. Under it, I write "Which Why broke" for every miss. If the naive guess beat my predictions, I say so plainly.
- I add each new failure type to `spe/failures.md`, continuing the F numbering.
- I add a "Proposed for round 6" table to the spec and write `spe/predictions/r05-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
- I update `spe/README.md` with the round's result paragraph and the rerun command.
- Commit: `SPE r05 learn: <the main lesson>`, then a local tag `spe-r05`.

## Rounds 6 and later
- Each round repeats the same five commits and the same gates.
- Before each round starts, I check every stop rule and cap. I also check that the proposals contain only items from the "alone" list.
- You are not awake to approve rounds 6 and later. For those rounds, the predict commit stands in for your approval. I write the plan and the prediction, check both against the caps, and commit them before any trial runs. You can audit every prediction against its timestamp in git.
- If the session compacts, I re-read `spe/README.md`, the latest plan, and the latest prediction log section before I continue.

## Git
- All commits and tags stay local. Nothing is pushed.
- Commit messages carry no Claude attribution lines, as your CLAUDE.md requires.

## Morning report (in chat)
- Which stop rule ended the loop, and the round it fired in.
- One headline line per round, with its numbers.
- Prediction accuracy per round as hits out of total, and whether my predictions beat the naive guess.
- New failure entries by F number.
- Open decisions that need you, each with the evidence behind it.
- Git state, meaning the list of local commits and tags, with nothing pushed.

The morning report section lists "One headline line per round, with its numbers." It also lists "Prediction accuracy per round as hits out of total", which shows the trend across rounds. It ends with "Open decisions that need you, each with the evidence behind it."
